story: Born Devavrata, son of King Shantanu and the river goddess Ganga, he vowed never to marry or take the throne so that his father could marry Satyavati. That terrible vow (bhishan pratigya) gave him the name Bhishma, and the gods granted him the power to choose the moment of his own death.
belief: Bhishma is honoured as the grand elder of the Kuru dynasty and a great teacher of dharma. His teachings to Yudhishthira from his deathbed of arrows fill whole books of the Mahabharata.
turns: He stayed silent while Draupadi was dragged into the court and humiliated. He carried off three princesses as brides for his half-brother, ruining Amba's life. He fought for the Kauravas even though he knew they were wrong.
facts: He lay on a bed of arrows for 58 days, waiting for Uttarayana before he chose to die.
Amba was reborn as Shikhandi to bring about his fall.
Bhishma Ashtami marks the day he left his body.
lessons: A vow should serve what's right, not replace it.
Silence in front of injustice is still a choice.
more: Tradition says the Vishnu Sahasranama was taught by him from his bed of arrows.
He was the eighth son of Ganga; she let the river take the other seven at birth to free them from a curse.
